name: When Companies Ruled the World
description: Merchant houses with their own armies, flags and colonies: how the charter company, the trust and the multinational took over the work of kings and states.

checkpoints.name: Bankers and charters
checkpoints.note: Before the great companies, banking families such as the Medici lent to kings and popes and showed how money could rule. Their methods of credit and branches prepared the ground for the chartered company.

checkpoints.name: Company-states
checkpoints.note: Kings gave merchants charters and monopolies, and the companies grew armies, forts and colonies. The English and Dutch East India Companies, the Virginia Company and the Hudson's Bay Company ran territories on three continents.

checkpoints.name: Trusts and empires of industry
checkpoints.note: Steel, electricity and oil gave rise to firms of a new scale. Krupp, Siemens and Standard Oil grew enormous, and in southern Africa, De Beers and Cecil Rhodes joined mining wealth with political power.

checkpoints.name: The age of the multinational
checkpoints.note: Cars, bananas, telephones and electronics produced firms with branches in many countries. Governments broke up some, such as the Bell System, and others, such as Ford, Toyota, Sony and Tata, became household names.
